name: monad_test
doc: Tests of the monad class. A test is a proposition about a constructor. Its proofs are instantiations: each one checks the property for the constructors it names, and says which part failed. A bool is a cast of the verdict, not a separate test.

types.name: Verdict
types.doc: Whether a constructor passed a test, and if it did not, the first part that failed.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: The first part that failed, absent when it passed.

functions.name: explain
functions.doc: The verdict on a constructor: whether it is a monad, with the reason it is not. A constructor passes only if it has both members and its laws hold. The reasons are `no_pure` and `no_bind` for a constructor missing a member, and otherwise the first law that fails on the samples: `left_identity`, `right_identity`, or `associativity`. Futures are not an input, since a future has no value until it arrives, so its laws cannot be run here.

functions.name: holds
functions.doc: Whether a constructor is a monad. The cast of `explain` down to its bool, so it has no proofs of its own.
